svg.title: AudioStash: how everything connects
svg.desc: The Android app, the API on a cloud server with Postgres and RabbitMQ, the download worker on a home PC, Cloudflare R2 storage, Clerk sign-in and public music APIs, with the nine steps of a song download.
svg.text: The planned production layout. Today all of it runs in Docker on your PC, and RustFS stands in for Cloudflare R2.
Email and password, or Google, Apple, GitHub,
Facebook. Keeps your account and each device's
session, and signs the session tokens.
Deezer genre charts, search, song tags, album art
The API uses them for charts and search, cached in memory. The worker uses Deezer and LRCLIB for tags and lyrics.
Docker · HTTPS for the phone, Tailscale for the PC
Read SQLite; ask the API for charts, downloads
Push: sends the outbox (your edits) to the API, in order.
Pull: fetches the change log after its cursor and applies it to SQLite.
Runs each time you open the app, on reconnect, on library.changed, after edits.
src/db/database.ts · the phone's own copy of the library
the library, pulled from the server
your edits, waiting for the next push
files already in the Music folder
a folder you pick, or app storage
After each complete sync, makes the Music
folder match the library: saves new and
changed songs, deletes removed ones, writes
playlists. Skips mobile data unless allowed.
Every /v1 route needs your Clerk session token, except the worker's.

g.text: /v1/catalog/*
charts, search, recommendations
/v1/downloads
start, list, cancel, retry, remove
/v1/sync/push, /pull
your edits in, library changes out
/v1/songs/file-urls
links to download song files
/v1/uploads
links to upload your own audio files
/v1/sessions
signed-in devices; sign one out
/v1/status, /events
is the worker online, live events (SSE)
/v1/worker/*
worker only, with WORKER_TOKEN
/health, /ready
no token; for Docker and uptime checks

svg.text: the change log, numbered in order
jobs waiting to go to RabbitMQ
a queue each for download.resolve and download.item
waits 30 s, 2 min or 10 min, then retries
events from the API and the worker
Takes jobs from RabbitMQ: up to 2 songs at once by default.
Changes data only through the API's /v1/worker/* routes,
and every call is safe to repeat after a crash.
A playlist, album or channel link becomes a list of songs.
The API then adds a download.item job for each new one.
src/jobs/item.ts · one song, in four stages
Probes the link or upload, or searches YouTube for a pick.
Tags from Deezer. Stops if it is already in the library.
yt-dlp fetches the best audio stream.
Progress goes out as live events.
ffmpeg converts only if needed, measures loudness.
Adds lyrics, cover art and tags.
Gets upload links from the API, puts the files in R2,
then tells the API the song is ready.
Download progress, and a heartbeat every 30 s,
go straight to RabbitMQ as events. After 90 s
with no heartbeat, the app shows the PC offline.
file storage that speaks the Amazon S3 protocol · RustFS stands in for it locally
Only the API holds the storage keys. The phone and the worker
reach it through presigned links the API signs. Songs keep
downloading to the phone while the PC is off.

g.text: You pick a song, paste a link or upload your own files. The app sends POST /v1/downloads
with an id it chose, so sending it twice is harmless.
One Postgres transaction saves the download and outbox rows: a job per new song, or a resolve job for a playlist.
The outbox relay sends each job to RabbitMQ, and marks it sent only once RabbitMQ confirms it has it.
RabbitMQ hands the job to the worker over Tailscale. If the PC is off, the job waits in its queue.
The worker claims the item and reports each stage through /v1/worker/*, sent with WORKER_TOKEN.
It uploads the audio and cover to R2, then reports the item complete. The API adds the song to the change log.
Each update goes out as an event through RabbitMQ, and the API forwards it to your phone's open SSE stream.
The library.changed event makes the phone sync. The new song lands in SQLite and shows in your library.
The mirror gets a link from /v1/songs/file-urls and saves the file from R2 into the Music folder.

svg.text: A failed job runs again from the start after 30 s, 2 min and 10 min. Then it goes to the dead queue and the song shows as failed.
A failure that a retry cannot fix, such as a deleted video, fails the song at once.

g.text: Outbox table
Jobs saved in the same transaction as the change that needs them. The relay sends them to RabbitMQ
afterwards, so a crash can never keep the change but lose its job.
RabbitMQ
A message broker: it holds jobs in queues until a worker takes them. Retry queues
delay a failed job; the dead queue keeps the jobs whose retries ran out.
Change log
library_changes gives every library change the next number. Each phone remembers the
last number it saw (its cursor) and pulls only what came after it.
Phone outbox
Edits you make on the phone apply locally at once and wait here until a push succeeds.
The server's applied_mutations table makes sure each one is applied only once.
Presigned link
A URL the API signs that allows uploading or downloading one file, for one hour.
It works without the storage keys, which stay on the server.
SSE
Server-Sent Events: one long HTTP response the API keeps writing events into.
The app keeps it open while it is on screen.
Mirror
Makes the Music folder match the library after each complete sync. The files are plain
audio files, so other music apps can play them too.
Tailscale
A private network between your own machines. The PC connects out to the server,
so nothing on the PC is open to the internet.
Tokens
The phone sends a Clerk session token, a signed JWT that expires after about a minute.
The worker sends WORKER_TOKEN, a long secret shared with the API.
packages/
Code the apps share: contracts (request shapes), core (matching, file paths), catalog
(music API clients), db (schema, migrations), messaging (RabbitMQ setup).
